projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: Everything I have built so far. Some of it is live, some is open code, and some is still private while I work on it.
projects.sovereign_desc: A coding agent that runs on your own computer. It plans a task, writes the code, checks the result and tries again if it fails. Every file change can be rolled back.
projects.awal_desc: A Tamazight–English dictionary with more than 10,000 entries that works without internet. Search in Tifinagh, Latin or Arabic script, and learn with quizzes, a verb conjugator and writing practice.
projects.asphalt_desc: The calculator I wanted when I worked on the road. It works out asphalt quantities by German standards (RStO 12, ZTV Asphalt), plans the trucks, shows the time left for compaction and creates the paving record as a PDF.
projects.chip8_desc: An emulator for CHIP-8, SUPER-CHIP and XO-CHIP with a built-in debugger: breakpoints, single steps, a memory editor, save states and rewind. It comes with its own assembler.
projects.graph_desc: Graph algorithms written from scratch in Java — Dijkstra, A*, PageRank, Louvain and more — and shown step by step as an animation in the browser.
projects.mosslight_desc: A cozy 2D fantasy game: a village with eight neighbours, errands to run, crafting, farming, fishing — and fighting only if you want to.
projects.graben_desc: A map app for crews digging near buried cables and pipes. It shows the lines in the standard colours, warns when you get close and records the route by GPS. Works offline.
projects.rebar_desc: Checks the spacing of reinforcement bars from a photo. It corrects the perspective, measures the gaps and marks every one that is outside the tolerance.
projects.architect_desc: Several AI agents that work as a team on local models: one plans, workers write code in parallel, a reviewer and a tester send mistakes back.
projects.shadow_desc: An assistant in the system tray. It looks at the screen with a local vision model and only speaks up when something changed and it has something useful to say. Nothing leaves the computer.
projects.paleo_desc: A field companion for fossil sites in Morocco that works offline: 22,667 fossil records on a satellite map, GPS logging, voice notes and a PDF report for each find.
projects.minigame_desc: 21 classic mini-games in one Android app, with a daily challenge, achievements and four languages — drawn directly, without a game engine.
projects.ethry_desc: A farming and adventure RPG. You take over an old farm, find a dragon egg and travel through six regions to renew an old pact with the dragons. It has 114 characters with daily routines, 81 quests, puzzle dungeons with bosses and a story told in 24 cutscenes.
projects.resonance_desc: A 2D action RPG with sword fights and an “Echo” boomerang that reveals hidden paths.
projects.neon_desc: Arcade mini-games in neon style to play with friends, right in the browser.
projects.checkers_desc: Checkers with a computer opponent that thinks several moves ahead, in different playing styles. With undo and saved games.
projects.ttt_desc: Boards up to 5×5, a computer opponent with difficulty levels and two-player games over the local network.
projects.platformer_desc: Five levels with double jump, wall jump and five kinds of enemies.
projects.shrub_desc: A website for a made-up garden company, first in plain HTML and then rebuilt in React with dark mode and a checked contact form.
projects.shoppy_desc: The front end of a small online shop — one of my first web projects.
projects.site_desc: Built without a framework: my own visitor statistics that only count after consent, a contact form with spam protection, an admin area and two languages.

about.title: About
about.p1: I learned discipline in a trade where one wrong measurement means tearing up a road. I write code with the same care.
about.p2_html: I'm Mehdi Lakhouane, an independent developer in Frankfurt. I came to Germany from Morocco in 2018, trained as a Straßenbauer (road builder) and taught myself software by building real things — project by project.
about.p3: Because I have stood in the trench myself, I build software for people who wear gloves and have no signal: tools that work offline, on a phone, in a hurry. The same thinking goes into my AI agents, which run on your own machine and keep your data there.
about.quote: “I built RebarSight because I watched a contractor break out fresh concrete after the rebar spacing was wrong.”
about.quote_note: Most of my projects start like this: with a problem I have seen myself.
about.pr1_desc: A project that stays on my hard drive helps nobody. I build things until they can be used.
about.pr2_desc: Python, React, Flutter, Godot, C++ — I learned each one because a project needed it.
about.pr3_desc: Site workers, language learners, people who care about privacy. Not imaginary users.

background.title: Background
background.self_desc: I learned software mainly by building the projects on this page, and I add courses where they help.
background.ausb_desc: Three years of vocational training in road construction: material calculations, logistics and exact work under real deadlines. It led directly to RebarSight, GrabenGeist and the Asphalt Calculator.
background.eng_desc: Taught me to think, write and structure ideas clearly — useful every day for documentation and game stories.
background.bac_desc: Sciences and languages — the starting point before I moved to Germany in 2018.
background.cert_note: Courses by Meta on Coursera. Each title opens the verified certificate.

datenschutz.p2: We use the following providers to deliver this website:

datenschutz.h3: 3. Data collected when visiting the website (server logs)
datenschutz.p3: When this website is accessed, technically necessary data (IP address, timestamp, URL accessed, referrer, user agent) is processed by our host. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest in secure operation). These logs are stored for a short time for security purposes.
datenschutz.p4: In your browser's local storage we only store your cookie consent decision and – only if you change them yourself using the buttons – your language choice and your choice of light or dark display. This storage is strictly necessary to respect your choices, not show the banner again and display the site the way you selected. No consent is required.
datenschutz.p5_html: Only with your explicit consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR, § 25(1) TTDSG) do we collect anonymous statistics about page views. We use no tracking cookies and share no data with third parties.
datenschutz.p5_li2: referrer (where you came from), if your browser sends it
datenschutz.p5_li3_html: approximate country (derived from the IP by Vercel, without storing the IP)
datenschutz.p5_li5_html: a daily-rotating, salted hash of IP + user agent as session ID. This hash cannot be traced back to your IP and expires after 24 h.
datenschutz.p5_footer_html: The IP address itself is not stored. The data is hosted on Supabase servers in the EU (Ireland).
datenschutz.p6: When you send a message via the contact form, we process the data you provide (name, email, message text) to handle your request. The legal basis is your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), which you give by actively ticking the checkbox. In addition, we store a daily-rotating hash of your IP for spam prevention (rate limiting); this can no longer be attributed after 24 hours. Messages are deleted after a maximum of 12 months, provided no further communication takes place. You can withdraw your consent at any time by sending us an email.
datenschutz.p7_html: The /admin area is only accessible to the site operator. Authentication is via a "magic link" through Supabase Auth. Only the email address and a session token are processed. Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR.
datenschutz.p8_li1: Reach measurement: aggregated up to 24 months, raw data deleted after 90 days.
datenschutz.p8_li2: Consent log: 3 years (retention obligation under Art. 7(1) GDPR).
